parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Chilliwack · Greendale
Greendale is an MLS® sub-area name in the City of Chilliwack. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it, and Published municipal records list no street-by-street boundary in official sources.

The closest official clues are the roads: Greendale Community Elementary is on Sumas Prairie Road, and the Great Blue Heron Nature Reserve is at the south end of Sumas Prairie Road in Greendale, along the Vedder River.
BC Transit’s route 55 loop runs between Vedder Rd and UFV, Yarrow and Greendale, which shows the road links into the area.

Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Greendale

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

The City of Chilliwack’s 2050 Official Community Plan, Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500, was adopted on December 16, 2025. It covers the whole city, including Greendale, and the City says it will be reviewed again in 2030.
The Agricultural Area Plan is Schedule B1 of the current Official Community Plan. It sets the City’s agricultural land policies for its farm areas, including Greendale.
Published municipal directories do not list a Greendale-specific neighbourhood plan separate from the Official Community Plan and the Agricultural Area Plan.

The Agricultural Area Plan says the City supports the protection and enhancement of designated agricultural land for agricultural purposes, and works with the Agricultural Land Commission on an Urban Containment Boundary.

The 2040 Official Community Plan, which the 2050 plan replaced, listed Greendale with Rosedale and Yarrow as Rural Settlements, with a policy to retain their existing boundaries and limit growth to existing development areas.
ALR: whether a parcel is in the ALR is set address by address, and Verify parcel-specific status for Greendale as a whole from an Agricultural Land Commission page.

The City says much of Chilliwack lies in the floodplain of the Fraser River to the north, the Vedder River to the south, the Sumas River to the west, or one of several creeks entering the valley from hillside areas.
The City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw No. 4519 sets construction elevation requirements for new development in the floodplain: the applicable Flood Construction Level plus 0.6 m of freeboard.

Within the ALR, on properties protected by standard dykes, Flood Construction Levels have generally been standardized at 1.2 m above the natural ground elevation, and the owner registers a covenant about flooding on title.
The City keeps a Fraser River Flood Response Plan, last revised March 25, 2026, with phases tied to Mission Gauge levels.
The City has an ongoing $30 million program to raise its dyke system.
The City of Chilliwack is one of the partners, with the Province, Abbotsford and three First Nations, in the Sumas River Flood Mitigation Collaborative Framework, signed on April 28, 2023.

FAQ
Where is Greendale?
Greendale is an MLS® sub-area name. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it, and Published municipal records list no street-by-street boundary in official sources.
Greendale Community Elementary is on Sumas Prairie Road, and the Great Blue Heron Nature Reserve is at the south end of Sumas Prairie Road, along the Vedder River.
Ask me if a specific address is in it.
How do I get around from Greendale?
BC Transit route 55 Yarrow–Greendale is a loop that serves Greendale on weekdays and Saturdays. No Sunday service is shown.
Its timing points are Vedder Rd at South Sumas Rd, the UFV Chilliwack campus, Yarrow Central Rd at Kehler St and Greendale.
